## Final checkpoint

**PR:** https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/72 (branch pushed, both success criteria verified passing)

**Important finding first:** the extracted document (`VERIDIAN_Architecture_v2.0_extracted.txt`, 564 lines) contains **zero** literal occurrences of "mode pill," "option chain," "chat input," or "machine language" — I grepped the full text to confirm. The Owner's Option 1/2 language is the Owner's own UX vocabulary, not sourced from the document. I anchored the amendments to the real closest sections instead: Stage 1 "User Input" (line 213-215), the Prompt Compiler Engine's "natural language intent to optimized machine prompt" (line 79), the Stage 4 Machine Prompt Builder (line 225-227), and the Browser Execution Engine (line 144) — and both amended phases carry an explicit "NOTE ON SOURCING" documenting this rather than fabricating a false citation.

**Phases amended:**
- **phase_2** — added a scope bullet + objective note establishing Stage 4 Machine Prompt Builder / Prompt Compiler Engine as the real machine-language-output contract that phase_5's two input surfaces must compile into (no new engine needed).
- **phase_5** — added a scope bullet with three concrete deliverables (mode-pill/option-chain component, free-text chat component, browser-FIRST/server-SECOND handoff), extended `integration_point` for the handoff via Gateway G05, and added a `success_criteria` item — explicitly distinguished from the existing Tier-5 `engine-server-escalation` item (escalation-on-insufficiency ≠ Owner's mandatory two-pass model).

**Phases checked and found unaffected (with reasoning):** phase_3 (governance applies uniformly regardless of input surface), phase_4 (guardrails already wrap the shared G05 boundary both passes use), phase_6 (cache keys on compiled content, not input surface), phase_7 (existing trace_id/span_id tracing already generic), phase_8 (concerns compilation quality, not staging), phase_9 (already generically scoped to any real G05 request), phase_10 (documents whatever phases 1-9 actually ship).

**phase_1 verified untouched** (`git diff` shows zero changes to its block) — it stays dispatched and in progress against compliance-tracker as instructed.

One YAML gotcha I hit and fixed along the way: two of the file's fields (`objective`, one `success_criteria` item) were unquoted plain scalars in the original, which can't contain a colon-space or trailing colon — my first draft broke `yaml.safe_load`. Fixed by using `--` in place of `:`, matching the file's existing convention, then re-validated clean.
